hypothesis: Eight 32-lane jobs run on one firmware context in one session, the client CCB wraps with a padding command, and each job is timed from the board counter.
prediction: timeline=0x8 and jobs=8; every job's 32 words as in the first job (w0=0x2e5ca990, w31=0x4775f521), guards 0x6d35a7c1; job 6 at write offset 0xb8 and ring line cccb_read=0x228 cccb_write=0x228, so the firmware followed the padding command without a context reset (events n=0); kccb_done=0xb after the cleanup (health check, MMUCACHE, eight KICKs, cleanup) and 0xd after the two power requests; per-job latency had no earlier measurement: a 32-lane job at 1,008 MHz was expected well under 1 ms, and a first job much slower than the others would point at cold MMU and system-level caches. Ring derivation: a job writes the CDM command (40-byte header and 96 bytes) and the timeline UPDATE (40 and 8), 184 bytes (0xb8) of the 1,024-byte ring; after five jobs the write offset is 920; the sixth CDM command needs its 136 bytes plus room for a 40-byte padding header, 176 bytes, and 104 remain, so the host writes a padding command (type 221, size 64) at 920 and restarts at 0, as upstream does (pvr_cccb.c:163-188). The write offsets after the jobs are 0xb8 ... 0x398 for jobs 1 to 5, then 0xb8, 0x170, 0x228.

conditions.counter: 24 MHz generic counter, one tick 41.7 ns

conclusion: Eight 32-lane jobs ran on one context in one firmware session; all 32 output words matched, with no firmware event or reset; the cleanup and the stop were acknowledged and the GPU powered off. The ring wrap with the padding command (never before read by the firmware from SunstoneOS) worked. Job 1 follows MMUCACHE and first fetches programs and input through the system-level cache; job 6 includes the firmware's read of the padding command and was the first job after the ring wrapped. A job's time includes the firmware's scheduling, the CDM work, the timeline UPDATE and its write reaching the CPU; done is the moment the timeline UPDATE becomes visible to the CPU, not the end of the compute work.
narrative: Set 29 had no time for the job (62.42 ms image time, 25.75 ms remainder covering preparation, job, cleanup, park and report). Image: apps/gpu-power-id/fw-start.c built with FWS_STOP and FWS_JOB gained FWS_JOBS=8 (default 1); the one-job build differs from the image qualified in set 29 in the timed spin, no tick wait in the job, MMUCACHE and cleanup loops, the new log lines, a job without its timeline reported in its KICK phase, and the never-kicked branch of the cleanup rule. Timing: kick is the counter read immediately before the MTS_SCHEDULE write, after its progress record and log line and a DSB SY; done is the counter at the first read of the timeline word equal to n in a spin of one counter read and one Normal-NC load per pass (no register access, clock lock, log line or yield); per-job log lines give ticks from kick to the spin's first read, the pass count and scheduler ticks crossed (a nonzero count marks a time a tick or service step may have lengthened); `first` includes the MTS_SCHEDULE read-back and its two log lines. MMUCACHE and cleanup waits no longer yield. Log lines: `GPU FWJ run n=6 ticks=... first=... passes=... os=... write=0xb8`; `GPU FWJ phases prepare=... publish=... mmu=... jobs=... cleanup=...`; `GPU FWS park ticks=...`; the job line gains jobs=. Each extra KICK adds about 235 bytes of log, about 2.3 KB in all, to about 13.6 KB of 16,128. Operating point: the vendor's top node (highest of gpu_opp_table, sun60iw2p1.dtsi:4736-4761 at kernel 2ac08e8c7; the others are 800, 600 and 400 MHz, 300 MHz is commented out); include/a733_gpu_opp.h holds it. Budget table: job submit (8 per session) costs the output refill and clean of one page, two CCCB command writes, one KCCB command, one MTS_SCHEDULE write and read-back, with no tick wait or status poll between submit and kick; the completion spin per pass costs one counter read and one Normal-NC timeline read; the control service per pass after done costs two interrupt-status reads, the kernel CCB control reads with their barriers and the counter-clock reads; the output check (8 per session) costs one page invalidate and 64 word reads. Completion is polled rather than interrupt-driven because the image has no qualified GPU interrupt handler (the interrupt path is qualified in the GPU service, checks/pvr-gpu-irq.c) and the wait is far shorter than a tick.

hypothesis: Host checks cover the eight-job ring, the session image and its worst-case log.
narrative: checks/pvr-cccb.c: eight two-command jobs through the 1,024-byte ring compared with upstream's bytes after every job: the padding command at 920 (type 221, size 64) before job 6, job 6 at 0, each KICK's write offset and wrap mask, and a firmware read offset still at job 5's start (736) when job 6 is written, leaving 839 bytes free for the 288 needed. Each job completes before the next is written, so the ring never waits for space in this session; the existing pressure cases cover the wait. apps/gpu-power-id/check.py --fw-session (fifteen cases) on the eight-job image with a firmware model that runs every KICK and follows the padding command: eight complete jobs (timeline 8, every job's words, kccb_done=0xb after the cleanup, the per-job, phase and park lines); a job that never completes at job 1, 5, 6 and 8 (earlier jobs complete, no cleanup, the stop powers the GPU off); a context reset at job 1, 5, 6 and 8 (cleanup sent, stop powers off); a reset whose job writes no timeline (job 6); a firmware that reads job 6's padding command, moves to 0 and stops; the clock passing the wait's end after job 5, during job 6's publish or while its commands are written (job 6 never kicked, the two forms of the never-kicked branch); less than 10 ms of the wait left after job 4 (outcome 6); the worst-case log under 16,128 bytes (eight jobs, a reset at job 8, no power acknowledgement; the model's timeline arrives on the spin's third counter read so the multi-pass spin runs). The one-job image (--fw-job) still passes its thirteen cases. Design-panel outcomes: the kick stamp is just before the MTS_SCHEDULE write; done comes from a spin on the timeline word alone; a repeat needs 10 ms of the 150 ms wait left; the phase and park times and the never-completes and reset cases at jobs 1, 5, 6 and 8 were kept against one reviewer because the step asks for the job's own time inside the first job's remainder and for those cases.

hypothesis: The failed-shutdown rules retain power and ownership in every case where the drain is not proven.
narrative: The native ELF checks model the firmware and platform power callbacks. They check retained power after failed idle polls, failed startup, refused control and collection failure after the OFF acknowledgement; plain OFF before firmware startup; and reject every GPU access after OFF begins. The corrected firmware-stop, first-job and eight-job native images built; fourteen selected stop cases, four job cases and two session cases passed. Build records, source hashes, ELF files and model results are under ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/gpu-recovery-20261025/. These establish software ordering; physical failure recovery and application operation remain unqualified for this revision. Stop budget: 300 ms total within the diagnostic's 2 s monitor, 200 ms for acknowledged shutdown and 100 ms for an admitted unacknowledged stop, shorter than the vendor's 500 ms per poll and upstream's 1 s per poll.
